overall_summary: View counts across all historical videos are extremely low (0 to 20 views), indicating low sample size and minimal algorithmic distribution so far. Patterns are difficult to confirm reliably, but slightly higher initial views on relatable daily digital habits (like phone numbers, chat histories, and old names) suggest the audience responds to modern, highly visual micro-milieu touchpoints.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos focusing on phone contacts, chat boxes, and stored names (e.g., 'आज भी फोन में तुम्हारा नाम सुरक्षित है' with 20 views, and 'नंबर पर अभी भी तेरी तस्वीर है' with 18 views) performed relatively better than abstract late-night thoughts.
winning_patterns.action: Continue focusing hooks on smartphone interactions, chat interfaces, and modern relationship relics.

weak_patterns.pattern: Abstract silence or overly poetic time-based hooks
weak_patterns.evidence: Hooks like 'रात के दो बजे' (12 views) or 'मेज पर रखी चाय ठंडी हो गई' (5 views) and 0-view videos with complex descriptions showed lower traction in this sample.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid purely atmospheric or cliché poetic openings; ground the hook in a specific, immediate modern action.

experiment: Testing if a specific visual digital realization (default profile picture after unblocking/blocking) outperforms saved-number hooks.
